strings.name: Paul Romer
strings.summary: Romer brought knowledge and innovation into long-run growth models, showing how non-rival ideas differ from ordinary scarce goods and how incentives shape research. He shared the 2018 economics Nobel and served as World Bank chief economist. Since joining Boston College in 2023, he has developed work on authenticating digital information.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 16 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Developed endogenous growth theory, emphasizing knowledge, innovation and institutions in long-run growth.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Chicago mathematics BS and economics PhD (1983).
strings.highlights.h1.title: Ideas within growth
strings.highlights.h1.text: Uses non-rival knowledge and innovation incentives to explain sustained growth.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Institutions and digital trust
strings.highlights.h2.text: Studies urban institutions, platform rules and authenticating digital-file origins.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Digital-authenticity work reported
strings.timeline.t1.text: Boston College described tools under development for trustworthy information sharing, not universal deployment.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Joined Boston College
strings.timeline.t2.text: Became Seidner University Professor and founded the Center for the Economics of Ideas.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Shared economics Nobel
strings.timeline.t3.text: Honored alongside William Nordhaus; Romer’s citation concerned technological innovation in long-run analysis.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Became World Bank chief economist
strings.timeline.t4.text: Took office in October; served until January 2018.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Joined New York University
strings.timeline.t5.text: Developed research on cities, institutions and growth.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Technological-change paper
strings.timeline.t6.text: Modeled endogenous technical progress through research choices and knowledge properties.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Increasing-returns research
strings.timeline.t7.text: Examined knowledge accumulation, increasing returns and long-run growth.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Doctorate and first faculty job
strings.timeline.t8.text: Completed Chicago’s doctorate before teaching at Rochester.
